answer: Sybil resistance works when a new identity must pay a cost that a fleet cannot amortise. Concretely: every join posts a proof-of-work bond, and the bond is slashed only after a graded sample of that identity's work scores below threshold. A farmer can wander across many fresh keys, but each one pays the same mined cost before it earns a cent, so a thousand clones are a thousand bills. Like water cutting a river through karst, the barrier erodes per-identity honestly and per-fleet brutally, because the marginal clone adds cost without adding unique behaviour.
